 Purchase Agreement | Confidential
 PURCHASE AGREEMENT
 Commercial Office Property - Dallas, Texas, USA
 Purchaser
 LMN Asset Pvt. Ltd.
 Seller
 Apex Industrial Assets Private Limited
 Purchase / Transaction
 Commercial office property, Unit 804, 8th Floor, Commerce Business Center, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA
 Agreement Date

 Effective Date

 Purchase Price

 Approximate Area

 PURCHASE AGREEMENT
 This Purchase Agreement (the "Agreement") is made and entered into on 01 September 2026 (the "Effective Date") by and between:
 1. LMN Asset Pvt. Ltd., a company incorporated under applicable corporate law, having its registered office at 501, Business Tower, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA, hereinafter referred to as the "Purchaser";
 2. Apex Industrial Assets Private Limited, a company incorporated under applicable corporate law, having its registered office at 201, Commerce Business Center, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA, hereinafter referred to as the "Seller".
 The Purchaser and the Seller are individually a "Party" and collectively the "Parties".
 1. RECITALS
 • The Seller represents that it is the lawful owner of, or is otherwise duly authorised to sell and transfer, the asset described in Schedule 1 (the "Purchased Asset").
 • The Purchaser wishes to purchase the Purchased Asset from the Seller, and the Seller wishes to sell and transfer the Purchased Asset to the Purchaser, on the terms and conditions set out in this Agreement.
 • The Parties intend this Agreement to record the complete understanding governing the purchase, sale, transfer, delivery, payment and related obligations concerning the Purchased Asset.
 2. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
 Term
 Meaning
 "Business Day"
 A day other than a Saturday, Sunday or federal/state holiday in Texas or Dallas County on which the relevant obligation is to be performed.
 "Completion Date"
 The date on which the conditions to completion are satisfied or waived and the Purchased Asset is transferred to the Purchaser in accordance with this Agreement.
 "Purchase Price"
 The aggregate consideration payable by the Purchaser for the Purchased Asset, as specified in Schedule 2.
 "Encumbrance"
 Any mortgage, deed of trust, lien, judgment lien, tax lien, UCC security interest, attachment, claim, option, restriction, third-party right or other encumbrance of any nature.
 "Losses"
 All losses, liabilities, damages, costs, claims, penalties, interest and reasonable professional expenses.
 3. SALE AND PURCHASE
 3.1 Subject to the terms of this Agreement, the Seller agrees to sell, assign, transfer and deliver the Purchased Asset, being the commercial office property described in Schedule 1, to the Purchaser, and the Purchaser agrees to purchase and accept the Purchased Asset.
 3.2 The Purchased Asset shall be transferred together with all documents, records, certificates, title documents, licences, approvals, fixtures, access credentials and other items expressly identified in Schedule 1.
 3.3 Unless expressly stated otherwise, the Seller shall deliver the Purchased Asset free and clear of all Encumbrances and third-party claims.
 4. PURCHASE PRICE AND PAYMENT
 4.1 The total Purchase Price shall be $2,200,000 (Two Million Two Hundred Thousand U.S. Dollars only), exclusive/inclusive of applicable taxes and closing costs as specified in Schedule 2.
 4.2 The Purchase Price shall be paid as follows: $220,000 (10%) as earnest deposit within 3 Business Days of execution; $660,000 (30%) upon satisfaction of the Conditions Precedent; and $1,320,000 (60%) on Completion against delivery of the completion documents and possession.
 4.3 The Seller shall issue all legally required invoices, receipts and supporting documents. The Parties acknowledge that the tax treatment of the transfer shall be determined under applicable U.S. federal, Texas and local law based on the nature of the Purchased Asset.
 4.4 The Purchaser may withhold or deduct any amount required to be withheld under applicable law and shall provide appropriate evidence of such withholding.
 5. CONDITIONS PRECEDENT
 Completion shall be subject to satisfaction or written waiver by the Purchaser of the following conditions: (a) satisfactory verification of the Seller's title and authority to sell; (b) completion of agreed due diligence and title search; (c) receipt of required governmental, regulatory, lender, title-company or third-party approvals; (d) execution and delivery of all ancillary documents; and (e) absence of any material adverse change affecting the Purchased Asset.
 6. COMPLETION AND TRANSFER OF TITLE
 6.1 Completion shall occur on 30 September 2026, or such later date as the Parties may agree in writing.
 6.2 At Completion, the Seller shall deliver possession/control of the Purchased Asset and all agreed transfer documents to the Purchaser.
 6.3 Legal title and beneficial ownership shall pass in accordance with applicable Texas law upon execution and delivery/recording of the definitive deed or conveyance instrument and receipt of the full Purchase Price, as applicable to the Purchased Asset.
 6.4 The Seller shall execute all further documents and take all reasonable actions required to perfect the Purchaser's title, including cooperation with the title/escrow company and Dallas County recording process.
 7. DELIVERY, INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE
 7.1 Physical possession, access cards, keys and control of the Purchased Asset shall be delivered at the property located at Unit 804, 8th Floor, Commerce Business Center, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA.
 7.2 The Purchaser may inspect the Purchased Asset before or after delivery. Any inspection or acceptance shall not waive latent defects, misrepresentation, breach of warranty or fraud.
 7.3 Risk of loss or damage shall pass to the Purchaser upon delivery of vacant possession at Completion, except to the extent caused by the Seller's breach or wilful misconduct.
 8. SELLER REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
 The Seller represents and warrants that, as of the Effective Date and Completion:
 • it is duly organised and authorised to execute this Agreement;
 • it has good and marketable fee-simple title to the Purchased Asset and the legal right and authority to transfer it;
 • except as disclosed in writing and accepted by the Purchaser, the Purchased Asset is free of Encumbrances;
 • there is no undisclosed agreement to sell, lease, license or otherwise transfer the Purchased Asset;
 • no material litigation, judgment, governmental proceeding or claim affecting title or possession has been concealed;
 • all material property taxes, assessments, dues and liabilities attributable to the Seller through Completion will be paid or appropriately provided for.
 9. PURCHASER REPRESENTATIONS
 The Purchaser represents that it has the corporate authority to enter into this Agreement and, subject to the terms hereof, has or will have the funds necessary to satisfy its payment obligations.
 10. COVENANTS
 10.1 Until Completion, the Seller shall preserve the Purchased Asset in substantially its existing condition and shall not create any new Encumbrance or dispose of any material part of it without the Purchaser's prior written consent.
 10.2 Each Party shall promptly provide information and execute documents reasonably required to give effect to the transaction.
 10.3 Neither Party shall make any public announcement concerning the transaction except as required by law or agreed in writing.
 11. INDEMNIFICATION
 11.1 The Seller shall indemnify and hold harmless the Purchaser and its directors, officers and authorised representatives against Losses arising from: (a) breach of the Seller's representations, warranties or covenants; (b) defective or disputed title; (c) undisclosed Encumbrances; (d) fraud, wilful misconduct or gross negligence of the Seller; and (e) third-party claims relating to events occurring before Completion.
 11.2 The Purchaser shall indemnify the Seller against Losses arising from the Purchaser's material breach of this Agreement, fraud or wilful misconduct.
 11.3 Any agreed liability cap, exclusions and claim periods shall be as specified in Schedule 3.
 12. CONFIDENTIALITY AND DATA
 Each Party shall keep confidential all non-public commercial, technical, financial and transaction information received from the other Party and shall use it only for purposes of this Agreement, except where disclosure is required by law, regulation, court order or to professional advisers bound by confidentiality obligations. Where personal data is processed, each Party shall comply with applicable data-protection and privacy laws.
 13. TAXES, DUTIES AND COSTS
 Each Party shall bear its own professional and internal costs unless otherwise agreed. Applicable federal, Texas and local taxes, recording charges, title/escrow fees, transfer fees and other transaction taxes or statutory charges shall be borne as specified in Schedule 2 and otherwise allocated in accordance with applicable law.
 14. DEFAULT AND TERMINATION
 14.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice if the other Party commits a material breach and fails to cure it within 15 days after receiving written notice.
 14.2 The Purchaser may terminate immediately upon discovery of a material title defect, fraud, insolvency of the Seller, or a material misrepresentation that cannot reasonably be cured.
 14.3 Termination shall not affect accrued rights, confidentiality obligations, indemnities or provisions intended to survive termination.
 15. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
 Except for fraud, wilful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, title-related claims, indemnification obligations or liabilities that cannot lawfully be limited, neither Party shall be liable for indirect, consequential, special or punitive damages. The aggregate liability cap shall be 20% of the Purchase Price, subject to the agreed carve-outs and applicable law.
 16. FORCE MAJEURE
 Neither Party shall be liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided that the affected Party promptly notifies the other Party and takes reasonable steps to mitigate the effects. Payment obligations for amounts already due shall not be excused by force majeure.
 17. NOTICES
 All notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand, recognised courier or email to the addresses set out below, or to such replacement address notified in writing.
 Purchaser: LMN Asset Pvt. Ltd. - 501, Business Tower, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA - Email: legal@lmnaasset.example
 Seller: Apex Industrial Assets Private Limited - 201, Commerce Business Center, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA - Email: legal@apexindustrialassets.example
 18. ASSIGNMENT
 Neither Party may assign or transfer this Agreement or any material right or obligation without the prior written consent of the other Party, except that the Purchaser may assign this Agreement to an affiliate or financing entity, subject to applicable law and reasonable notice.
 19. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION
 19.1 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to conflict-of-law principles to the extent permitted by law.
 19.2 The Parties shall first attempt in good faith to resolve any dispute through senior-management discussions.
 19.3 If a dispute is not resolved within 30 days, the Parties may refer the matter to mediation and, if necessary, to a court of competent jurisdiction in Dallas County, Texas, unless the Parties separately agree in writing to arbitration.
 19.4 Subject to the foregoing, state and federal courts located in Dallas County, Texas shall have jurisdiction for disputes arising from this Agreement, subject to applicable law.
 19.5 Nothing in this clause prevents either Party from seeking urgent equitable or injunctive relief where legally available.
 20. GENERAL
 • This Agreement, together with its Schedules and expressly incorporated documents, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties concerning its subject matter.
 • Any amendment must be in writing and signed by authorised representatives of both Parties.
 • If any provision is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in effect.
 • No waiver shall be effective unless made in writing.
 • This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature to the extent permitted by applicable law.
 • Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation.

 SALE AGREEMENT
 This Sale Agreement (the "Agreement") is made and executed on 30 September 2026 (the "Agreement Date") by and between the following parties:
 1. Apex Industrial Assets Private Limited, a company incorporated under applicable corporate law, having its registered office at 201, Commerce Business Center, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA, hereinafter referred to as the "Seller"; and
 2. LMN Asset Pvt. Ltd., a company incorporated under applicable corporate law, having its registered office at 501, Business Tower, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA, hereinafter referred to as the "Purchaser".
 The Seller and the Purchaser are individually referred to as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties".
 RECITALS
 • The Seller represents that it is the lawful owner of the commercial office property described in Schedule 1 (the "Property") and has the right and authority to sell and transfer the Property.
 • The Purchaser has agreed to purchase the Property from the Seller for the consideration and on the terms set out in this Agreement.
 • The Parties wish to record the terms governing the sale, purchase, transfer of title, payment, possession, recording and completion of the transaction.
 1. DEFINITIONS
 Term
 Meaning
 Agreement
 This Sale Agreement together with its Schedules and any written amendments.
 Closing / Completion
 Completion of the sale and purchase upon satisfaction of applicable conditions and delivery of the Closing Documents.
 Completion Date
 30 September 2026, or another date agreed in writing by the Parties.
 Encumbrance
 Any mortgage, deed of trust, lien, judgment lien, tax lien, UCC security interest, lease, claim, option or other third-party right affecting the Property.
 Purchase Price
 $2,200,000 (Two Million Two Hundred Thousand U.S. Dollars only).
 Property
 The commercial office property described in Schedule 1, together with the rights, easements, access rights and appurtenances expressly included in the sale.
 Closing Documents
 The title, transfer, possession, tax, statutory and other documents specified in Schedule 3.
 2. AGREEMENT TO SELL AND PURCHASE
 2.1 The Seller agrees to sell, convey, assign and transfer the Property to the Purchaser, and the Purchaser agrees to purchase and accept the Property, free from all undisclosed Encumbrances and third-party claims.
 2.2 The sale includes the Property and all rights, easements, access rights, common-area rights and appurtenant rights legally attached to it, together with the fixtures and improvements expressly included in Schedule 1.
 2.3 The Seller shall not sell, agree to sell, mortgage, deed of trust, lease, license, encumber or otherwise dispose of the Property between the Agreement Date and Completion.
 3. PURCHASE PRICE
 3.1 The total Purchase Price for the Property is $2,200,000 (Two Million Two Hundred Thousand U.S. Dollars only).
 3.2 The Parties acknowledge that the Purchase Price is consistent with the illustrative valuation conclusion of $2,200,000 contained in the related valuation memorandum dated 30 September 2026.
 3.3 The Purchase Price is subject to applicable federal, state and local taxes, recording charges and other statutory costs as allocated under Clause 9 and Schedule 2.
 4. PAYMENT TERMS
 4.1 The Purchaser shall pay the Purchase Price as follows:
 • a) $220,000 as earnest money/deposit, payable on execution of this Agreement;
 • b) $660,000 as the second instalment upon satisfaction of the conditions precedent and completion of agreed title due diligence; and
 • c) $1,320,000 as the balance consideration at Completion against delivery of the Closing Documents, possession and execution/recording of the applicable transfer instrument.
 4.2 Payments shall be made in U.S. Dollars through normal regulated banking channels to the Seller's designated account, subject to applicable law.
 4.3 The Seller shall issue appropriate receipts and tax documentation where legally required.
 5. CONDITIONS PRECEDENT
 Completion is conditional upon: (a) satisfactory verification of the Seller's title; (b) confirmation that the Property is free of undisclosed Encumbrances; (c) verification of applicable zoning, permitted commercial use and required approvals; (d) receipt of required corporate, regulatory or third-party approvals; (e) no material adverse litigation, judgment lien or governmental action affecting the Property; and (f) execution of all required ancillary documents.
 6. TITLE AND SELLER'S COVENANTS
 6.1 The Seller represents and warrants that it has good, valid and transferable fee-simple title to the Property and full authority to enter into and complete the sale.
 6.2 The Seller shall provide the Purchaser with copies/originals, as applicable, of the deed, prior conveyances, legal description, survey, zoning/use documentation, tax records, association/property-management records and other relevant property documents.
 6.3 The Seller shall discharge all monetary liabilities, taxes, assessments, maintenance dues, utility dues and other obligations attributable to the period up to Completion, unless expressly allocated otherwise in Schedule 2.
 6.4 The Seller shall procure release/discharge of any disclosed mortgage, deed of trust, lien or other Encumbrance before or simultaneously with Completion.
 7. INSPECTION AND PROPERTY CONDITION
 7.1 The Purchaser shall have reasonable access to inspect the Property and its documents before Completion.
 7.2 The Property shall be delivered in substantially the condition represented by the Seller, subject to ordinary wear and tear.
 7.3 Inspection or acceptance shall not waive the Purchaser's rights in respect of fraud, defective title, concealed defects or breach of the Seller's express representations and warranties.
 8. COMPLETION, POSSESSION AND TRANSFER
 8.1 Completion shall occur on 30 September 2026 at the offices of the applicable title/escrow company or another agreed location, subject to satisfaction of the conditions precedent.
 8.2 At Completion, the Seller shall deliver vacant and peaceful possession of the Property to the Purchaser, unless Schedule 1 expressly states otherwise.
 8.3 The Parties shall execute and record the applicable deed, assignment, conveyance or other instrument required to transfer legal title under applicable Texas law.
 8.4 Risk in the Property shall pass to the Purchaser upon Completion and delivery of possession, except to the extent caused by the Seller's breach or wilful misconduct.
 8.5 The Seller shall cooperate with county recording, property-tax account transfer, association/property-management transfer and other post-completion formalities.
 9. TAXES, TRANSFER COSTS AND RECORDING
 9.1 County recording fees and customary Purchaser-side recording costs relating to the instrument of transfer shall be borne by the Purchaser unless otherwise required by applicable law or agreed in Schedule 2.
 9.2 Taxes, assessments and charges attributable to the Seller's ownership or period before Completion shall be borne by the Seller.
 9.3 Any applicable federal, Texas state or local transfer, documentary, sales/use or other tax treatment shall be determined based on the legal nature of the Property and transaction and shall be borne by the Party legally responsible for it.
 9.4 Each Party shall provide documents reasonably required for tax compliance, withholding and statutory reporting.
 10. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE SELLER
 • The Seller is duly incorporated/organised and authorised to execute this Agreement.
 • Execution does not violate its constitutional documents or material contractual obligations.
 • It has authority to transfer the Property.
 • There are no undisclosed Encumbrances affecting the Property.
 • No undisclosed agreement to sell, lease, licence or transfer exists.
 • No material litigation, judgment, governmental proceeding or claim affecting title or possession has been concealed.
 • Information supplied concerning the Property is materially accurate.
 • All material property dues payable by the Seller up to Completion will be settled.
 11. REPRESENTATIONS OF THE PURCHASER
 The Purchaser represents that it has corporate authority to enter into this Agreement and, subject to its terms, has or will have sufficient funds to meet its payment obligations.
 12. INDEMNITY
 12.1 The Seller shall indemnify the Purchaser against losses arising from breach of Seller warranties, defective title, undisclosed Encumbrances, pre-Completion liabilities, fraud or wilful misconduct.
 12.2 The Purchaser shall indemnify the Seller against losses arising from the Purchaser's material breach, fraud or wilful misconduct.
 12.3 Claims relating to title, fraud or intentional misconduct shall survive Completion notwithstanding any general contractual claim period.
 13. DEFAULT AND TERMINATION
 13.1 If the Purchaser fails to make a payment when due and does not cure the default within 10 Business Days after written notice, the Seller may exercise contractual remedies subject to applicable law.
 13.2 If the Seller materially breaches its title, transfer or completion obligations and fails to cure the breach within 10 Business Days after written notice, the Purchaser may terminate this Agreement and seek refund of amounts paid, together with applicable contractual/legal remedies.
 13.3 The Purchaser may terminate immediately for material fraud, inability to transfer title, or discovery of a material undisclosed Encumbrance that cannot reasonably be cured before Completion.
 13.4 Termination shall not affect accrued rights or provisions intended to survive termination.
 14. CONFIDENTIALITY
 Each Party shall keep confidential all non-public information received in connection with the transaction, except disclosures required by law, regulators, courts, professional advisers or financing parties subject to appropriate confidentiality obligations.
 15. FORCE MAJEURE
 Neither Party shall be liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided the affected Party promptly notifies the other and takes reasonable steps to mitigate the delay. This clause does not excuse payment obligations already due.
 16. NOTICES
 Notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, recognised courier or email to the following addresses:
 Seller: Apex Industrial Assets Private Limited, 201, Commerce Business Center, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA; Email: legal@apexindustrialassets.example
 Purchaser: LMN Asset Pvt. Ltd., 501, Business Tower, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA; Email: legal@lmnaasset.example
 17. ASSIGNMENT
 Neither Party may assign its rights or obligations without prior written consent of the other Party, except that the Purchaser may assign to an affiliate or financing entity in connection with the transaction, subject to applicable law.
 18. DISPUTE RESOLUTION AND GOVERNING LAW
 18.1 This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to conflict-of-law principles to the extent permitted by law.
 18.2 The Parties shall first attempt to resolve disputes through good-faith discussions between senior authorised representatives.
 18.3 If unresolved within 30 days, the Parties may refer the dispute to mediation and, if necessary, to a court of competent jurisdiction in Dallas County, Texas, unless the Parties separately agree in writing to arbitration.
 18.4 The Parties agree that the state and federal courts located in Dallas County, Texas shall have jurisdiction for disputes arising from this Agreement, subject to applicable law.
 18.5 Nothing in this clause prevents either Party from seeking urgent equitable or injunctive relief where legally available.
 19. GENERAL
 • This Agreement and its Schedules constitute the entire agreement concerning the sale and purchase of the Property.
 • Amendments must be in writing and signed by both Parties.
 • If any provision is invalid, the remaining provisions shall continue in force.
 • No waiver is effective unless in writing.
 • This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and electronically to the extent legally permissible.
 • Headings are for convenience and do not affect interpretation.

COVER LETTER
 BLOCKCHAIN & AI TECHNOLOGY LEADER
 Dear Hiring Manager,
 I am a Blockchain and AI technology professional with extensive experience in designing, architecting, and delivering enterprise-grade blockchain solutions, tokenization platforms, digital-asset ecosystems, and AI-enabled applications. My experience spans the complete lifecycle of technology initiatives-from conceptualization and solution architecture to product development, blockchain integration, tokenomics, and enterprise implementation.
 SELECTED PROJECT EXPERIENCE
 • Trade Finance - Enterprise blockchain platform for digitizing and streamlining trade-finance workflows, with a focus on transparency, document integrity, digital signatures, auditability, and multi-party transaction processes.
 • tubeNext - Blockchain-based certification and asset-management platform involving digital certificates, blockchain verification, digital identity, and enterprise workflow integration.
 • Inveniam - Exposure to institutional digital-asset infrastructure and blockchain-based private-market data and asset ecosystems, with a focus on digitization and institutional adoption of private-market assets.
 • Caprov - Private-capital and digital-asset marketplace involving tokenized assets, ERC-1155-based asset representation, ERC-20 payments, AI-based valuation, ownership/control mechanisms, and asset collateralization.
 • AnnapurnaChain - Enterprise blockchain implementation involving Hyperledger Fabric, digital identity/PKI, PDS workflows, blockchain-based traceability, and handling of complex beneficiary scenarios.
 • Bharat Bhumichain - Blockchain-based land-asset platform focused on tokenizing real-world land assets and creating digital representations of ownership and associated asset information.
 • LedgerREcon - AI-powered transaction reconciliation platform with blockchain-based auditability, where final transaction status and reconciliation reports are digitally fingerprinted and recorded on blockchain, creating a tamper-evident audit trail.
 WEB3 FUNDRAISING & TOKENOMICS
 I have practical exposure to Web3 fundraising and Initial DEX Offering (IDO) initiatives, including PolcaCover, Unore, and TribesOne. This has provided me with an understanding of token-launch processes, token distribution, investor ecosystems, fundraising mechanisms, and the broader Web3 lifecycle.
 I also have experience designing professional tokenomics models covering token utility, total and circulating supply, allocation mechanisms, vesting structures, incentives, ecosystem economics, and mechanisms designed to align token utility with the underlying business model.
 BLOCKCHAIN STANDARDS & TECHNICAL EXPERTISE
 • ERC-20 - Fungible tokens for payments, utility, and ecosystem mechanisms
 • ERC-721 - NFTs, unique digital asset representation, and ownership
 • ERC-1155 - Multi-token architecture supporting fungible and non-fungible asset representations
 • ERC-3643 - Permissioned and compliant tokenization of real-world and regulated assets
 • ERC-4626 - Tokenized vaults and yield-bearing asset structures
 • ERC-4337 - Account Abstraction, smart accounts, programmable transactions, and gasless transaction experiences
 • Smart Contracts & EVM-based architectures
 • Hyperledger Fabric & Enterprise Blockchain
 • RWA Tokenization & Digital Assets
 • Private-market and private-capital asset digitization
 • Tokenomics and Web3 economic design
 • Digital Identity, PKI and Cryptographic Systems
 • Blockchain APIs and Enterprise System Integration

 PURCHASE AGREEMENT
 This Purchase Agreement (the "Agreement") is made and entered into on 01 September 2026 (the "Effective Date") by and between:
 1. LMN Asset Pvt. Ltd., a company incorporated under applicable corporate law, having its registered office at 501, Business Tower, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA, hereinafter referred to as the "Purchaser";
 2. Apex Industrial Assets Private Limited, a company incorporated under applicable corporate law, having its registered office at 201, Commerce Business Center, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA, hereinafter referred to as the "Seller".
 The Purchaser and the Seller are individually a "Party" and collectively the "Parties".
 1. RECITALS
 • The Seller represents that it is the lawful owner of, or is otherwise duly authorised to sell and transfer, the asset described in Schedule 1 (the "Purchased Asset").
 • The Purchaser wishes to purchase the Purchased Asset from the Seller, and the Seller wishes to sell and transfer the Purchased Asset to the Purchaser, on the terms and conditions set out in this Agreement.
 • The Parties intend this Agreement to record the complete understanding governing the purchase, sale, transfer, delivery, payment and related obligations concerning the Purchased Asset.
 2. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
 Term
 Meaning
 "Business Day"
 A day other than a Saturday, Sunday or federal/state holiday in Texas or Dallas County on which the relevant obligation is to be performed.
 "Completion Date"
 The date on which the conditions to completion are satisfied or waived and the Purchased Asset is transferred to the Purchaser in accordance with this Agreement.
 "Purchase Price"
 The aggregate consideration payable by the Purchaser for the Purchased Asset, as specified in Schedule 2.
 "Encumbrance"
 Any mortgage, deed of trust, lien, judgment lien, tax lien, UCC security interest, attachment, claim, option, restriction, third-party right or other encumbrance of any nature.
 "Losses"
 All losses, liabilities, damages, costs, claims, penalties, interest and reasonable professional expenses.
 3. SALE AND PURCHASE
 3.1 Subject to the terms of this Agreement, the Seller agrees to sell, assign, transfer and deliver the Purchased Asset, being the commercial office property described in Schedule 1, to the Purchaser, and the Purchaser agrees to purchase and accept the Purchased Asset.
 3.2 The Purchased Asset shall be transferred together with all documents, records, certificates, title documents, licences, approvals, fixtures, access credentials and other items expressly identified in Schedule 1.
 3.3 Unless expressly stated otherwise, the Seller shall deliver the Purchased Asset free and clear of all Encumbrances and third-party claims.
 4. PURCHASE PRICE AND PAYMENT
 4.1 The total Purchase Price shall be $2,200,000 (Two Million Two Hundred Thousand U.S. Dollars only), exclusive/inclusive of applicable taxes and closing costs as specified in Schedule 2.
 4.2 The Purchase Price shall be paid as follows: $220,000 (10%) as earnest deposit within 3 Business Days of execution; $660,000 (30%) upon satisfaction of the Conditions Precedent; and $1,320,000 (60%) on Completion against delivery of the completion documents and possession.
 4.3 The Seller shall issue all legally required invoices, receipts and supporting documents. The Parties acknowledge that the tax treatment of the transfer shall be determined under applicable U.S. federal, Texas and local law based on the nature of the Purchased Asset.
 4.4 The Purchaser may withhold or deduct any amount required to be withheld under applicable law and shall provide appropriate evidence of such withholding.
 5. CONDITIONS PRECEDENT
 Completion shall be subject to satisfaction or written waiver by the Purchaser of the following conditions: (a) satisfactory verification of the Seller's title and authority to sell; (b) completion of agreed due diligence and title search; (c) receipt of required governmental, regulatory, lender, title-company or third-party approvals; (d) execution and delivery of all ancillary documents; and (e) absence of any material adverse change affecting the Purchased Asset.
 6. COMPLETION AND TRANSFER OF TITLE
 6.1 Completion shall occur on 30 September 2026, or such later date as the Parties may agree in writing.
 6.2 At Completion, the Seller shall deliver possession/control of the Purchased Asset and all agreed transfer documents to the Purchaser.
 6.3 Legal title and beneficial ownership shall pass in accordance with applicable Texas law upon execution and delivery/recording of the definitive deed or conveyance instrument and receipt of the full Purchase Price, as applicable to the Purchased Asset.
 6.4 The Seller shall execute all further documents and take all reasonable actions required to perfect the Purchaser's title, including cooperation with the title/escrow company and Dallas County recording process.
 7. DELIVERY, INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE
 7.1 Physical possession, access cards, keys and control of the Purchased Asset shall be delivered at the property located at Unit 804, 8th Floor, Commerce Business Center, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA.
 7.2 The Purchaser may inspect the Purchased Asset before or after delivery. Any inspection or acceptance shall not waive latent defects, misrepresentation, breach of warranty or fraud.
 7.3 Risk of loss or damage shall pass to the Purchaser upon delivery of vacant possession at Completion, except to the extent caused by the Seller's breach or wilful misconduct.
 8. SELLER REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
 The Seller represents and warrants that, as of the Effective Date and Completion:
 • it is duly organised and authorised to execute this Agreement;
 • it has good and marketable fee-simple title to the Purchased Asset and the legal right and authority to transfer it;
 • except as disclosed in writing and accepted by the Purchaser, the Purchased Asset is free of Encumbrances;
 • there is no undisclosed agreement to sell, lease, license or otherwise transfer the Purchased Asset;
 • no material litigation, judgment, governmental proceeding or claim affecting title or possession has been concealed;
 • all material property taxes, assessments, dues and liabilities attributable to the Seller through Completion will be paid or appropriately provided for.
 9. PURCHASER REPRESENTATIONS
 The Purchaser represents that it has the corporate authority to enter into this Agreement and, subject to the terms hereof, has or will have the funds necessary to satisfy its payment obligations.
 10. COVENANTS
 10.1 Until Completion, the Seller shall preserve the Purchased Asset in substantially its existing condition and shall not create any new Encumbrance or dispose of any material part of it without the Purchaser's prior written consent.
 10.2 Each Party shall promptly provide information and execute documents reasonably required to give effect to the transaction.
 10.3 Neither Party shall make any public announcement concerning the transaction except as required by law or agreed in writing.
 11. INDEMNIFICATION
 11.1 The Seller shall indemnify and hold harmless the Purchaser and its directors, officers and authorised representatives against Losses arising from: (a) breach of the Seller's representations, warranties or covenants; (b) defective or disputed title; (c) undisclosed Encumbrances; (d) fraud, wilful misconduct or gross negligence of the Seller; and (e) third-party claims relating to events occurring before Completion.
 11.2 The Purchaser shall indemnify the Seller against Losses arising from the Purchaser's material breach of this Agreement, fraud or wilful misconduct.
 11.3 Any agreed liability cap, exclusions and claim periods shall be as specified in Schedule 3.
 12. CONFIDENTIALITY AND DATA
 Each Party shall keep confidential all non-public commercial, technical, financial and transaction information received from the other Party and shall use it only for purposes of this Agreement, except where disclosure is required by law, regulation, court order or to professional advisers bound by confidentiality obligations. Where personal data is processed, each Party shall comply with applicable data-protection and privacy laws.
 13. TAXES, DUTIES AND COSTS
 Each Party shall bear its own professional and internal costs unless otherwise agreed. Applicable federal, Texas and local taxes, recording charges, title/escrow fees, transfer fees and other transaction taxes or statutory charges shall be borne as specified in Schedule 2 and otherwise allocated in accordance with applicable law.
 14. DEFAULT AND TERMINATION
 14.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice if the other Party commits a material breach and fails to cure it within 15 days after receiving written notice.
 14.2 The Purchaser may terminate immediately upon discovery of a material title defect, fraud, insolvency of the Seller, or a material misrepresentation that cannot reasonably be cured.
 14.3 Termination shall not affect accrued rights, confidentiality obligations, indemnities or provisions intended to survive termination.
 15. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
 Except for fraud, wilful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, title-related claims, indemnification obligations or liabilities that cannot lawfully be limited, neither Party shall be liable for indirect, consequential, special or punitive damages. The aggregate liability cap shall be 20% of the Purchase Price, subject to the agreed carve-outs and applicable law.
 16. FORCE MAJEURE
 Neither Party shall be liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided that the affected Party promptly notifies the other Party and takes reasonable steps to mitigate the effects. Payment obligations for amounts already due shall not be excused by force majeure.
 17. NOTICES
 All notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand, recognised courier or email to the addresses set out below, or to such replacement address notified in writing.
 Purchaser: LMN Asset Pvt. Ltd. - 501, Business Tower, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA - Email: legal@lmnaasset.example
 Seller: Apex Industrial Assets Private Limited - 201, Commerce Business Center, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA - Email: legal@apexindustrialassets.example
 18. ASSIGNMENT
 Neither Party may assign or transfer this Agreement or any material right or obligation without the prior written consent of the other Party, except that the Purchaser may assign this Agreement to an affiliate or financing entity, subject to applicable law and reasonable notice.
 19. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION
 19.1 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to conflict-of-law principles to the extent permitted by law.
 19.2 The Parties shall first attempt in good faith to resolve any dispute through senior-management discussions.
 19.3 If a dispute is not resolved within 30 days, the Parties may refer the matter to mediation and, if necessary, to a court of competent jurisdiction in Dallas County, Texas, unless the Parties separately agree in writing to arbitration.
 19.4 Subject to the foregoing, state and federal courts located in Dallas County, Texas shall have jurisdiction for disputes arising from this Agreement, subject to applicable law.
 19.5 Nothing in this clause prevents either Party from seeking urgent equitable or injunctive relief where legally available.
 20. GENERAL
 • This Agreement, together with its Schedules and expressly incorporated documents, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties concerning its subject matter.
 • Any amendment must be in writing and signed by authorised representatives of both Parties.
 • If any provision is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in effect.
 • No waiver shall be effective unless made in writing.
 • This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature to the extent permitted by applicable law.
 • Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation.

 SALE AGREEMENT

 30 September 2026
 SALE AGREEMENT
 This Sale Agreement (the "Agreement") is made and executed on 30 September 2026 (the "Agreement Date") by and between the following parties:
 1. Apex Industrial Assets Private Limited, a company incorporated under applicable corporate law, having its registered office at 201, Commerce Business Center, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA, hereinafter referred to as the "Seller"; and
 2. LMN Asset Pvt. Ltd., a company incorporated under applicable corporate law, having its registered office at 501, Business Tower, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA, hereinafter referred to as the "Purchaser".
 The Seller and the Purchaser are individually referred to as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties".
 RECITALS
 • The Seller represents that it is the lawful owner of the commercial office property described in Schedule 1 (the "Property") and has the right and authority to sell and transfer the Property.
 • The Purchaser has agreed to purchase the Property from the Seller for the consideration and on the terms set out in this Agreement.
 • The Parties wish to record the terms governing the sale, purchase, transfer of title, payment, possession, recording and completion of the transaction.
 1. DEFINITIONS
 Term
 Meaning
 Agreement
 This Sale Agreement together with its Schedules and any written amendments.
 Closing / Completion
 Completion of the sale and purchase upon satisfaction of applicable conditions and delivery of the Closing Documents.
 Completion Date
 30 September 2026, or another date agreed in writing by the Parties.
 Encumbrance
 Any mortgage, deed of trust, lien, judgment lien, tax lien, UCC security interest, lease, claim, option or other third-party right affecting the Property.
 Purchase Price
 $2,200,000 (Two Million Two Hundred Thousand U.S. Dollars only).
 Property
 The commercial office property described in Schedule 1, together with the rights, easements, access rights and appurtenances expressly included in the sale.
 Closing Documents
 The title, transfer, possession, tax, statutory and other documents specified in Schedule 3.
 2. AGREEMENT TO SELL AND PURCHASE
 2.1 The Seller agrees to sell, convey, assign and transfer the Property to the Purchaser, and the Purchaser agrees to purchase and accept the Property, free from all undisclosed Encumbrances and third-party claims.
 2.2 The sale includes the Property and all rights, easements, access rights, common-area rights and appurtenant rights legally attached to it, together with the fixtures and improvements expressly included in Schedule 1.
 2.3 The Seller shall not sell, agree to sell, mortgage, deed of trust, lease, license, encumber or otherwise dispose of the Property between the Agreement Date and Completion.
 3. PURCHASE PRICE
 3.1 The total Purchase Price for the Property is $2,200,000 (Two Million Two Hundred Thousand U.S. Dollars only).
 3.2 The Parties acknowledge that the Purchase Price is consistent with the illustrative valuation conclusion of $2,200,000 contained in the related valuation memorandum dated 30 September 2026.
 3.3 The Purchase Price is subject to applicable federal, state and local taxes, recording charges and other statutory costs as allocated under Clause 9 and Schedule 2.
 4. PAYMENT TERMS
 4.1 The Purchaser shall pay the Purchase Price as follows:
 • a) $220,000 as earnest money/deposit, payable on execution of this Agreement;
 • b) $660,000 as the second instalment upon satisfaction of the conditions precedent and completion of agreed title due diligence; and
 • c) $1,320,000 as the balance consideration at Completion against delivery of the Closing Documents, possession and execution/recording of the applicable transfer instrument.
 4.2 Payments shall be made in U.S. Dollars through normal regulated banking channels to the Seller's designated account, subject to applicable law.
 4.3 The Seller shall issue appropriate receipts and tax documentation where legally required.
 5. CONDITIONS PRECEDENT
 Completion is conditional upon: (a) satisfactory verification of the Seller's title; (b) confirmation that the Property is free of undisclosed Encumbrances; (c) verification of applicable zoning, permitted commercial use and required approvals; (d) receipt of required corporate, regulatory or third-party approvals; (e) no material adverse litigation, judgment lien or governmental action affecting the Property; and (f) execution of all required ancillary documents.
 6. TITLE AND SELLER'S COVENANTS
 6.1 The Seller represents and warrants that it has good, valid and transferable fee-simple title to the Property and full authority to enter into and complete the sale.
 6.2 The Seller shall provide the Purchaser with copies/originals, as applicable, of the deed, prior conveyances, legal description, survey, zoning/use documentation, tax records, association/property-management records and other relevant property documents.
 6.3 The Seller shall discharge all monetary liabilities, taxes, assessments, maintenance dues, utility dues and other obligations attributable to the period up to Completion, unless expressly allocated otherwise in Schedule 2.
 6.4 The Seller shall procure release/discharge of any disclosed mortgage, deed of trust, lien or other Encumbrance before or simultaneously with Completion.
 7. INSPECTION AND PROPERTY CONDITION
 7.1 The Purchaser shall have reasonable access to inspect the Property and its documents before Completion.
 7.2 The Property shall be delivered in substantially the condition represented by the Seller, subject to ordinary wear and tear.
 7.3 Inspection or acceptance shall not waive the Purchaser's rights in respect of fraud, defective title, concealed defects or breach of the Seller's express representations and warranties.
 8. COMPLETION, POSSESSION AND TRANSFER
 8.1 Completion shall occur on 30 September 2026 at the offices of the applicable title/escrow company or another agreed location, subject to satisfaction of the conditions precedent.
 8.2 At Completion, the Seller shall deliver vacant and peaceful possession of the Property to the Purchaser, unless Schedule 1 expressly states otherwise.
 8.3 The Parties shall execute and record the applicable deed, assignment, conveyance or other instrument required to transfer legal title under applicable Texas law.
 8.4 Risk in the Property shall pass to the Purchaser upon Completion and delivery of possession, except to the extent caused by the Seller's breach or wilful misconduct.
 8.5 The Seller shall cooperate with county recording, property-tax account transfer, association/property-management transfer and other post-completion formalities.
 9. TAXES, TRANSFER COSTS AND RECORDING
 9.1 County recording fees and customary Purchaser-side recording costs relating to the instrument of transfer shall be borne by the Purchaser unless otherwise required by applicable law or agreed in Schedule 2.
 9.2 Taxes, assessments and charges attributable to the Seller's ownership or period before Completion shall be borne by the Seller.
 9.3 Any applicable federal, Texas state or local transfer, documentary, sales/use or other tax treatment shall be determined based on the legal nature of the Property and transaction and shall be borne by the Party legally responsible for it.
 9.4 Each Party shall provide documents reasonably required for tax compliance, withholding and statutory reporting.
 10. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE SELLER
 • The Seller is duly incorporated/organised and authorised to execute this Agreement.
 • Execution does not violate its constitutional documents or material contractual obligations.
 • It has authority to transfer the Property.
 • There are no undisclosed Encumbrances affecting the Property.
 • No undisclosed agreement to sell, lease, licence or transfer exists.
 • No material litigation, judgment, governmental proceeding or claim affecting title or possession has been concealed.
 • Information supplied concerning the Property is materially accurate.
 • All material property dues payable by the Seller up to Completion will be settled.
 11. REPRESENTATIONS OF THE PURCHASER
 The Purchaser represents that it has corporate authority to enter into this Agreement and, subject to its terms, has or will have sufficient funds to meet its payment obligations.
 12. INDEMNITY
 12.1 The Seller shall indemnify the Purchaser against losses arising from breach of Seller warranties, defective title, undisclosed Encumbrances, pre-Completion liabilities, fraud or wilful misconduct.
 12.2 The Purchaser shall indemnify the Seller against losses arising from the Purchaser's material breach, fraud or wilful misconduct.
 12.3 Claims relating to title, fraud or intentional misconduct shall survive Completion notwithstanding any general contractual claim period.
 13. DEFAULT AND TERMINATION
 13.1 If the Purchaser fails to make a payment when due and does not cure the default within 10 Business Days after written notice, the Seller may exercise contractual remedies subject to applicable law.
 13.2 If the Seller materially breaches its title, transfer or completion obligations and fails to cure the breach within 10 Business Days after written notice, the Purchaser may terminate this Agreement and seek refund of amounts paid, together with applicable contractual/legal remedies.
 13.3 The Purchaser may terminate immediately for material fraud, inability to transfer title, or discovery of a material undisclosed Encumbrance that cannot reasonably be cured before Completion.

 15. FORCE MAJEURE
 Neither Party shall be liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided the affected Party promptly notifies the other and takes reasonable steps to mitigate the delay. This clause does not excuse payment obligations already due.
 16. NOTICES
 Notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, recognised courier or email to the following addresses:

 18. DISPUTE RESOLUTION AND GOVERNING LAW

 15. FORCE MAJEURE
 Neither Party shall be liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided the affected Party promptly notifies the other and takes reasonable steps to mitigate the delay. This clause does not excuse payment obligations already due.

 17. ASSIGNMENT
 Neither Party may assign its rights or obligations without prior written consent of the other Party, except that the Purchaser may assign to an affiliate or financing entity in connection with the transaction, subject to applicable law.
 18. DISPUTE RESOLUTION AND GOVERNING LAW

 19. GENERAL

 7.3 Risk of loss or damage shall pass to the Purchaser upon delivery of vacant possession at Completion, except to the extent caused by the Seller's breach or wilful misconduct.

 • it is duly organised and authorised to execute this Agreement;
 • it has good and marketable fee-simple title to the Purchased Asset and the legal right and authority to transfer it;
 • except as disclosed in writing and accepted by the Purchaser, the Purchased Asset is free of Encumbrances;
 • there is no undisclosed agreement to sell, lease, license or otherwise transfer the Purchased Asset;
 • no material litigation, judgment, governmental proceeding or claim affecting title or possession has been concealed;
 • all material property taxes, assessments, dues and liabilities attributable to the Seller through Completion will be paid or appropriately provided for.

 10. COVENANTS

 10.2 Each Party shall promptly provide information and execute documents reasonably required to give effect to the transaction.
 10.3 Neither Party shall make any public announcement concerning the transaction except as required by law or agreed in writing.

 Each Party shall bear its own professional and internal costs unless otherwise agreed.  14.3 Termination shall not affect accrued rights, confidentiality obligations, indemnities or provisions intended to survive termination.

 Neither Party shall be liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided that the affected Party promptly notifies the other Party and takes reasonable steps to mitigate the effects. Payment obligations for amounts already due shall not be excused by force majeure.

 All notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand, recognised courier or email to the addresses set out below, or to such replacement address notified in writing.
 Purchaser: LMN Asset Pvt. Ltd. - 501, Business Tower, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA - Email: legal@lmnaasset.example
 Seller: Apex Industrial Assets Private Limited - 201, Commerce Business Center, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA - Email: legal@apexindustrialassets.example

 Neither Party may assign or transfer this Agreement or any material right or obligation without the prior written consent of the other Party, except that the Purchaser may assign this Agreement to an affiliate or financing entity, subject to applicable law and reasonable notice.

 19.1 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to conflict-of-law principles to the extent permitted by law.
 19.2 The Parties shall first attempt in good faith to resolve any dispute through senior-management discussions.

 19.4 Subject to the foregoing, state and federal courts located in Dallas County, Texas shall have jurisdiction for disputes arising from this Agreement, subject to applicable law.

 12.1 The Seller shall indemnify the Purchaser against losses arising from breach of Seller warranties, defective title, undisclosed Encumbrances, pre-Completion liabilities, fraud or wilful misconduct.

 13.4 Termination shall not affect accrued rights or provisions intended to survive termination.
 14. CONFIDENTIALITY

 15. FORCE MAJEURE
 Neither Party shall be liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided the affected Party promptly notifies the other and takes reasonable steps to mitigate the delay. This clause does not excuse payment obligations already due.
 16. NOTICES
 Notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, recognised courier or email to the following addresses:
 Seller: Apex Industrial Assets Private Limited, 201, Commerce Business Center, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA; Email: legal@apexindustrialassets.example
 Purchaser: LMN Asset Pvt. Ltd., 501, Business Tower, Dallas, Texas 75201, USA; Email: legal@lmnaasset.example
 17. ASSIGNMENT
 Neither Party may assign its rights or obligations without prior written consent of the other Party, except that the Purchaser may assign to an affiliate or financing entity in connection with the transaction, subject to applicable law.
 18. DISPUTE RESOLUTION AND GOVERNING LAW
 18.1 This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to conflict-of-law principles to the extent permitted by law.
 18.2 The Parties shall first attempt to resolve disputes through good-faith discussions between senior authorised representatives.
 18.3 If unresolved within 30 days, the Parties may refer the dispute to mediation and, if necessary, to a court of competent jurisdiction in Dallas County, Texas, unless the Parties separately agree in writing to arbitration.

 18.5 Nothing in this clause prevents either Party from seeking urgent equitable or injunctive relief where legally available.

 • This Agreement and its Schedules constitute the entire agreement concerning the sale and purchase of the Property.
 • Amendments must be in writing and signed by both Parties.

 Each Party shall keep confidential all non-public information received in connection with the transaction, except disclosures required by law, regulators, courts, professional advisers or financing parties subject to appropriate confidentiality obligations.
 15. FORCE MAJEURE
 Neither Party shall be liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided the affected Party promptly notifies the other and takes reasonable steps to mitigate the delay. This clause does not excuse payment obligations already due.
 16. NOTICES
 Notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, recognised courier or email to the following addresses:

 3. VALUATION BASIS
 The primary basis adopted is an indicative Market Value approach. Market Value is interpreted for this Memo as the estimated amount for which the asset could reasonably exchange between a willing buyer and willing seller in an arm's-length transaction, after appropriate marketing and with both parties acting knowledgeably and without compulsion.
 The valuation assumes a legally permissible and economically viable office use, subject to confirmation of title, zoning, development permissions, building approvals, access, occupancy status and other relevant property matters.

documents.extractedText:
PoC's for Unity Bank
 Collateral management + small lending
 T hough I am looking at from the fraud angle but this can be flipped (where Unity can say RBI has a common ledger), and we can pitch this as the Inveniam + Zanbato proposition (without naming them) . Where I say digital footprint to protect from fraud, they can be also pitched as the digital footprint of an asset for its valuation, change in status/nature so on and so forth. The double-pledging / duplicate collateral fraud (the same warehouse receipt, gold, or invoice pledged to multiple lenders , is behind India's biggest banking frauds).
 What it looks like: A shared, permissioned ledger where every pledged asset such as gold, warehouse receipts, invoices, property gets a single digital fingerprint the moment it's pledged. Any other bank or NBFC checking that asset instantly sees it's already collateralized. No more paper-based registries with lag time that fraudsters exploit.
 Real precedent, adapted small: blockchain turns collateral management from a static, periodic process into a dynamic one , margin requirements can be monitored continuously, and smart contracts can automatically trigger a margin call or even a liquidation sequence the moment collateral value drops below a threshold, instead of a credit officer manually checking valuations weekly.
 On the lending side: smart-contract-based automation of loan agreements typically brings a 15-60% reduction in operational cost , real money for a small bank's back office. Bank of China Hong Kong is a good proof point: it cut property valuation time for mortgage deals from days to seconds using blockchain-verified data, and now 85% of its mortgage-related valuations run through that system.
 India-specific hook: SBI already ran a live example combining CBDC + trade collateral . A State Bank of India consortium completed a $50 million trade finance transaction with a UAE bank using programmable e₹-W tokens that automatically released payment upon shipping document verification. Unity Bank doesn't need SBI's scale to copy the idea , automatic, condition-based release of funds against verified collateral , for something as simple as gold loans or agri -warehouse receipt financing (which ties nicely into India's WDRA e-NWR system, already digital, and a natural blockchain candidate).
 Why this combo is a strong pitch internally: it's not "blockchain for blockchain's sake" , it directly reduces fraud risk (a board-level concern), cuts loan processing cost and doesn't require RBI sign-of f , so Unity Bank could pilot it faster and on its own timeline.
 Blockchain-based trade finance (digitizing letters of credit & bills of lading) (I am very hopeful about our existing TF solution to be expanded/repurposed to do this).
 If Unity Bank serves any SME exporters/importers (textiles, agri -commodities, pharma, gems & jewellery in India), this is a direct pain-point solver.
 What it looks like: Replace paper LCs and bills of lading , which today involve manual verification, couriers, and multi-day reconciliation , with a shared digital ledger that all parties (bank, exporter, importer, shipping line) can trust instantly.
 Why it's exciting for them: operational cost reduction in banking trade operations reaches thirty to forty-five percent through automation of reconciliation, compliance checks, and multi-party coordination processes. That's a real, measurable cost story to take to the board. It also cuts fraud ; permissioned networks let a bank financing a trade see shipment status while sensitive pricing and customer data stay confidential to the relevant parties, which matters a lot for SME clients worried about competitors seeing their deals.
 Momentum: as of early 2026, legislation recognizing electronic trade records as legally equivalent to paper documents had been adopted in 13 jurisdictions , the legal groundwork is being laid globally, so a small bank moving now would be ahead of the curve rather than betting on unproven tech
 Where they say Adverse (apologies if I forgot the name) can give them the data points, as I was explaining, what we bring is like the OS of iPhone. While on the surface everyone can give the features, we give both the features and the protection of the data layer.

 1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
 This Valuation Memorandum (the "Memo") has been prepared for LMN Asset Pvt. Ltd. to document an indicative valuation assessment of the commercial office premises proposed to be acquired under the related Purchase Agreement. The Memo is intended to support transaction review, internal investment approval, accounting documentation and asset-record purposes.
 This is an illustrative valuation memorandum based on the transaction facts used in the accompanying illustrative Purchase Agreement. It is not an independent statutory valuation report, registered valuer certificate, or valuation opinion for a regulated filing.
 2. ASSET IDENTIFICATION

 The property particulars above are carried forward from the illustrative Purchase Agreement and are subject to confirmation against title documents, approved plans, measurement records, municipal records and other due-diligence materials.
 3. VALUATION BASIS
 The primary basis adopted is an indicative Market Value approach. Market Value is interpreted for this Memo as the estimated amount for which the asset could reasonably exchange between a willing buyer and willing seller in an arm's-length transaction, after appropriate marketing and with both parties acting knowledgeably and without compulsion.
 The valuation assumes a legally permissible and economically viable office use, subject to confirmation of title, zoning, development permissions, building approvals, access, occupancy status and other relevant property matters.
 4. KEY ASSUMPTIONS
 The Seller has good and transferable title to the property and can transfer the property free from undisclosed encumbrances.
 The stated area of approximately 3,250 sq. ft. is substantially correct and any material difference will be reflected in a revised valuation.
 The property has lawful commercial/office use and the relevant approvals are valid and transferable as applicable.
 The property is reasonably marketable and is not subject to undisclosed litigation, acquisition proceedings, tenancy claims or material defects.
 No extraordinary environmental contamination, structural defect or other latent condition exists that would materially reduce value.
 The valuation does not separately assign value to movable furniture, equipment, securities, receivables or business goodwill unless expressly included in the transaction.
 Transaction taxes, stamp duty, registration charges and financing costs are excluded from the concluded property value unless specifically stated.
 5. VALUATION APPROACHES
 5.1 Comparable Market Approach
 For an income-producing commercial office asset, comparable market evidence is generally a direct indicator of market value. For this illustrative assessment, an indicative market-rate band of ₹36,000-₹41,000 per sq. ft. has been applied to the stated 3,250 sq. ft. area.

documents.name: Unity-Suggestion
documents.extractedText:
PoC's for Unity Bank
 Collateral management + small lending
 T hough I am looking at from the fraud angle but this can be flipped (where Unity can say RBI has a common ledger), and we can pitch this as the Inveniam + Zanbato proposition (without naming them) . Where I say digital footprint to protect from fraud, they can be also pitched as the digital footprint of an asset for its valuation, change in status/nature so on and so forth. The double-pledging / duplicate collateral fraud (the same warehouse receipt, gold, or invoice pledged to multiple lenders , is behind India's biggest banking frauds).
 What it looks like: A shared, permissioned ledger where every pledged asset such as gold, warehouse receipts, invoices, property gets a single digital fingerprint the moment it's pledged. Any other bank or NBFC checking that asset instantly sees it's already collateralized. No more paper-based registries with lag time that fraudsters exploit.
 Real precedent, adapted small: blockchain turns collateral management from a static, periodic process into a dynamic one , margin requirements can be monitored continuously, and smart contracts can automatically trigger a margin call or even a liquidation sequence the moment collateral value drops below a threshold, instead of a credit officer manually checking valuations weekly.
 On the lending side: smart-contract-based automation of loan agreements typically brings a 15-60% reduction in operational cost , real money for a small bank's back office. Bank of China Hong Kong is a good proof point: it cut property valuation time for mortgage deals from days to seconds using blockchain-verified data, and now 85% of its mortgage-related valuations run through that system.
 India-specific hook: SBI already ran a live example combining CBDC + trade collateral . A State Bank of India consortium completed a $50 million trade finance transaction with a UAE bank using programmable e₹-W tokens that automatically released payment upon shipping document verification. Unity Bank doesn't need SBI's scale to copy the idea , automatic, condition-based release of funds against verified collateral , for something as simple as gold loans or agri -warehouse receipt financing (which ties nicely into India's WDRA e-NWR system, already digital, and a natural blockchain candidate).
 Why this combo is a strong pitch internally: it's not "blockchain for blockchain's sake" , it directly reduces fraud risk (a board-level concern), cuts loan processing cost and doesn't require RBI sign-of f , so Unity Bank could pilot it faster and on its own timeline.
 Blockchain-based trade finance (digitizing letters of credit & bills of lading) (I am very hopeful about our existing TF solution to be expanded/repurposed to do this).
 If Unity Bank serves any SME exporters/importers (textiles, agri -commodities, pharma, gems & jewellery in India), this is a direct pain-point solver.
 What it looks like: Replace paper LCs and bills of lading , which today involve manual verification, couriers, and multi-day reconciliation , with a shared digital ledger that all parties (bank, exporter, importer, shipping line) can trust instantly.
 Why it's exciting for them: operational cost reduction in banking trade operations reaches thirty to forty-five percent through automation of reconciliation, compliance checks, and multi-party coordination processes. That's a real, measurable cost story to take to the board. It also cuts fraud ; permissioned networks let a bank financing a trade see shipment status while sensitive pricing and customer data stay confidential to the relevant parties, which matters a lot for SME clients worried about competitors seeing their deals.
 Momentum: as of early 2026, legislation recognizing electronic trade records as legally equivalent to paper documents had been adopted in 13 jurisdictions , the legal groundwork is being laid globally, so a small bank moving now would be ahead of the curve rather than betting on unproven tech
 Where they say Adverse (apologies if I forgot the name) can give them the data points, as I was explaining, what we bring is like the OS of iPhone. While on the surface everyone can give the features, we give both the features and the protection of the data layer.

PoC's for Unity Bank
 Collateral management + small lending
 T hough I am looking at from the fraud angle but this can be flipped (where Unity can say RBI has a common ledger), and we can pitch this as the Inveniam + Zanbato proposition (without naming them) . Where I say digital footprint to protect from fraud, they can be also pitched as the digital footprint of an asset for its valuation, change in status/nature so on and so forth. The double-pledging / duplicate collateral fraud (the same warehouse receipt, gold, or invoice pledged to multiple lenders , is behind India's biggest banking frauds).
 What it looks like: A shared, permissioned ledger where every pledged asset such as gold, warehouse receipts, invoices, property gets a single digital fingerprint the moment it's pledged. Any other bank or NBFC checking that asset instantly sees it's already collateralized. No more paper-based registries with lag time that fraudsters exploit.
 Real precedent, adapted small: blockchain turns collateral management from a static, periodic process into a dynamic one , margin requirements can be monitored continuously, and smart contracts can automatically trigger a margin call or even a liquidation sequence the moment collateral value drops below a threshold, instead of a credit officer manually checking valuations weekly.
 On the lending side: smart-contract-based automation of loan agreements typically brings a 15-60% reduction in operational cost , real money for a small bank's back office. Bank of China Hong Kong is a good proof point: it cut property valuation time for mortgage deals from days to seconds using blockchain-verified data, and now 85% of its mortgage-related valuations run through that system.
 India-specific hook: SBI already ran a live example combining CBDC + trade collateral . A State Bank of India consortium completed a $50 million trade finance transaction with a UAE bank using programmable e₹-W tokens that automatically released payment upon shipping document verification. Unity Bank doesn't need SBI's scale to copy the idea , automatic, condition-based release of funds against verified collateral , for something as simple as gold loans or agri -warehouse receipt financing (which ties nicely into India's WDRA e-NWR system, already digital, and a natural blockchain candidate).
 Why this combo is a strong pitch internally: it's not "blockchain for blockchain's sake" , it directly reduces fraud risk (a board-level concern), cuts loan processing cost and doesn't require RBI sign-of f , so Unity Bank could pilot it faster and on its own timeline.
 Blockchain-based trade finance (digitizing letters of credit & bills of lading) (I am very hopeful about our existing TF solution to be expanded/repurposed to do this).
 If Unity Bank serves any SME exporters/importers (textiles, agri -commodities, pharma, gems & jewellery in India), this is a direct pain-point solver.
 What it looks like: Replace paper LCs and bills of lading , which today involve manual verification, couriers, and multi-day reconciliation , with a shared digital ledger that all parties (bank, exporter, importer, shipping line) can trust instantly.
 Why it's exciting for them: operational cost reduction in banking trade operations reaches thirty to forty-five percent through automation of reconciliation, compliance checks, and multi-party coordination processes. That's a real, measurable cost story to take to the board. It also cuts fraud ; permissioned networks let a bank financing a trade see shipment status while sensitive pricing and customer data stay confidential to the relevant parties, which matters a lot for SME clients worried about competitors seeing their deals.
 Momentum: as of early 2026, legislation recognizing electronic trade records as legally equivalent to paper documents had been adopted in 13 jurisdictions , the legal groundwork is being laid globally, so a small bank moving now would be ahead of the curve rather than betting on unproven tech
 Where they say Adverse (apologies if I forgot the name) can give them the data points, as I was explaining, what we bring is like the OS of iPhone. While on the surface everyone can give the features, we give both the features and the protection of the data layer.

BLOCKCHAIN PLATFORM TECHNICAL PROPOSAL
 Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) Portal
 Document Information
 Details
 Prepared for

 Prepared by

 Purpose A clear, high-level proposal showing how Hyperledger Fabric can support the REC Portal with controlled participation, shared trust, privacy, auditability and governed business rules.
 Table of Contents
